rationale: I SHOT THE TOWN BEFORE PLANNING IT again - wide at a clear summer afternoon (day 13, 16.9h, cloud 0.39), at a spring night, at a rainy morning, plus the Courtyard quarter - and the summer afternoon says something no ledger entry has ever said. THE COURTYARD FLOOR IS EVENLY LIT AT FOUR O'CLOCK. A five-cell terrace runs the whole west side of a walled square and throws nothing across the paving. I grepped it rather than trusting the picture: `sunVec()` is the one light vector, `shadowF()/shSpread()/shOffset()` are a written and tested hardness trio, `dialThrow(h)` already solves exactly 'where does a point h above the ground land, in cells', and the comment at SH_KNEE counts NINE cast shadows in this town - trees, benches, the barrow, the shed, the sundial, the boat, the mill wheel, people. Every one of them is an OBJECT. Not one BUILDING casts. The whole vocabulary is built and the walls simply never call it, so an hour of the day currently changes the town's TINT and nothing about its SHAPE. That is the biggest thing a viewer meets in the first ten seconds, it is rung 4a by name (an hour nobody has seen - not a new hour on the clock but a new hour in the picture), and it is Roofs & skyline x CONNECT, the emptiest cell in the grid, in the domain that has waited longest: #130 gave every house its own eave and made the skyline ragged, and nothing downstream has ever read that difference at ground level. b140 makes the roofline the shadow line. I have priced the two failure modes into the brief - cost (cast from wall RUNS, not per cell; the ground is a CACHE and this must be live, like drawCloudShade) and double-darkening (nearShadow, cloud shade and applyLight all already multiply). It goes FIRST with 90 minutes and a stated 150-300 line diff.
